question: What is the primary purpose of human digestion?

options.A: Breaking down food into small molecules for absorption
options.B: Storing excess vitamins in the skeletal system
options.C: Filtering waste products from the urinary bladder
options.D: Generating red blood cells for systemic circulation

explanation: Digestion turns large food items into tiny particles that can easily pass through the intestinal wall into the blood. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why must complex food molecules undergo structural changes inside the body?

options.A: Complex molecules block the normal flow of blood through organs
options.B: The stomach cannot hold solid food for more than a few minutes
options.C: Unchanged food molecules immediately trigger severe immune reactions
options.D: Large molecules are too big to cross the intestinal lining into blood

explanation: Nutrients need to be small and soluble before they can slip through the gut wall and travel to nourish body tissues. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h1)

question: What name is given to the chewed mass of food ready for swallowing?
explanation: Teeth and saliva work together in the mouth to shape chewed food into a smooth ball called a bolus. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h2)

question: How does the mechanical churning of the stomach help chemical digestion?

options.A: It neutralizes all stomach acid to protect the intestinal lining
options.B: It increases the surface area of food exposed to digestive enzymes
options.C: It freezes food particles to make them easier to dissolve
options.D: It directly converts large protein chains into individual amino acids

explanation: Breaking food into smaller physical pieces gives enzymes more exposed surface to work on, speeding up chemical breakdown. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which substance begins the chemical breakdown of starches in the oral cavity?
explanation: Saliva contains an enzyme called amylase that starts breaking down complex starches right inside the mouth. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of hydrochloric acid in the stomach?

options.A: Helping to denature tough protein structures in food
options.B: Providing the acidic environment required for pepsin to work
options.C: Converting complex fats directly into fatty acids without enzymes
options.D: Killing harmful bacteria swallowed along with food

explanation: Stomach acid helps activate enzymes and kill germs, but fat breakdown relies on specific lipases and bile, not acid alone. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main role of segmentation movements in the small intestine?

options.A: Creating new enzymes to replace worn-out proteins
options.B: Back-and-forth mixing of chyme with digestive juices
options.C: Absorbing water to prevent dehydration in the colon
options.D: Pushing waste material rapidly backward toward the stomach

explanation: Segmentation sloshes chyme back and forth, ensuring thorough mixing with enzymes and contact with the gut wall. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h4)

question: What term describes the wave-like muscle contractions that move food forward?
explanation: Peristalsis involves ring-like muscles squeezing behind the food mass to push it along the digestive tract. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h4)

question: Where does the greatest amount of nutrient absorption occur in the body?
explanation: The inner lining of the small intestine is covered in tiny projections called villi, making it the primary site for absorbing nutrients. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why do many pregnant women experience sluggish digestion and heartburn during gestation?

options.A: The growing fetus completely blocks the production of all digestive enzymes
options.B: Rapid maternal weight gain destroys the villi in the small intestine
options.C: Increased stomach acid production dissolves the esophageal sphincter
options.D: Elevated progesterone levels relax smooth muscle in the digestive tract

explanation: Pregnancy hormones relax smooth muscles throughout the body, slowing down gut motility and leading to common issues like heartburn. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h5)
